evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` check only requires positive, changed manager PIDs and changed nonempty invocation IDs. It does not require the manager before/after observations to come from the same guest boot, so a guest reboot can satisfy this check without exercising a manager-only restart; a later reboot can still satisfy the separate `boot_id_changed` check. Requiring nonempty equal boot IDs around the manager restart closes that false-positive path and is a routine correctness fix for the intended check.
